questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

I like my new office.

options.text: I am liking my new office.
My new office was liked by me.
My new office has been liked by me.
My new office is liked by me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**My new office is liked by me**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and 'I' is the subject and '**my** new office' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'I' of the active voice becomes the object 'me', the object 'my new office' becomes the subject.
 
• The passive format "'is + V3 (liked)" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4*.*

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Ravish likes chocolate.

options.text: Chocolate was liked by Ravish.
Chocolate is liked by Ravish.
Chocolate were liked by Ravish.
Chocolate is being liked by Ravish.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the original sentence,** "likes"** is in the **simple present **tense, so **we need to maintain** the same tense in the passive voice.
 
• **When changing **a sentence from active to passive voice, the **object** of the active sentence (here "chocolate")** becomes the subject** of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb **'like'** **changes **to **'is liked'** to match the tense and the passive structure.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: '*Chocolate is liked by Ravish.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **"Chocolate was liked by Ravish." **- This uses the past tense ("was liked"), which changes the original tense of the sentence.
 
• **"Chocolate were liked by Ravish." **- This is grammatically incorrect because "were liked" should be used with plural subjects, and "chocolate" is singular.
 
• **"Chocolate is being liked by Ravish." **- The phrase "is being liked" suggests an ongoing action, which changes the tense and the meaning of the original sentence. "Like" is also a stative verb, which doesn't usually use continuous (progressive) tenses.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

Ravi will play the match.

options.text: The match is played by Ravi.
The match will have been played by Ravi.
The match will be playing by Ravi.
The match will be played by Ravi.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Ravi will play the match."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the match" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "will play" to "will be played" (future simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Ravi."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The match will be played by Ravi."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The match is played by Ravi." – This option uses the present simple passive instead of the future simple passive.
 
• **Option 2: **"The match will have been played by Ravi." – This option uses the future perfect passive, which is incorrect in this context.
 
• **Option 3: **"The match will be playing by Ravi." – This option is grammatically incorrect as it incorrectly uses the future continuous tense in passive form.

questions.question: Describe how you will tell your friends that someone has picked Suman’s pocket in passive voice.
